blocks.content: The CAG shall be the most important officer under the Constitution of India.

rows: Has no control over money issuance from Consolidated Fund
Money cannot be drawn from Exchequer without CAG approval
Executes role primarily as Auditor General after money is spent
Executes powers of both Comptroller as well as Auditor General
Must be a member of the House of Commons

items: CAG does NOT hold office during the pleasure of the President; removal requires a parliamentary address on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, similar to a Supreme Court judge.
CAG is ineligible for further office under the Government of India or any State government after ceasing to hold office.
Unlike the British CAG, the Indian CAG acts primarily as an Auditor General and has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
CAG acts as the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at both the Centre and State levels.
The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to parliamentary vote.
CAG submits three audit reports to the President: Audit Report on Appropriation Accounts, Audit Report on Finance Accounts, and Audit Report on Public Undertakings.
CAG serves as a friend, philosopher, and guide to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.
